longForm.overview:
The Thermometer emoji is the activity-coded tag - the thermometer tradition, the recreational cue, and the universal "thermometer moment" tag. Where 🎮 reads as gaming-coded energy and ⚽ reads as sports-coded energy, the Thermometer captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate activity-coded energy - a "thermometer reveal" tag or a "weather-coded" reveal.

The activity cue borrows from thermometer tradition and the modern thermometer-coded aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as thermometer-coded rather than literal.

What separates the Thermometer emoji from the rest of the weather family is the specific thermometer register. The emoji is not saying 'generic activity' (🎮) but rather 'thermometer-coded thermometer,' which carries a specific recreational, weather, or hobby specificity.

In real-world usage 🌡️ Thermometer lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate activity energy. A partner sends it on a "temp" moment. A friend sends it on a "activity" reveal. A coworker sends it on a "temp" tag. The temp cue is what makes the emoji feel activity-coded - it is not just 'a moment,' it is 'temp-coded energy.'

In dating 🌡️ Thermometer works as a soft-coded temp tag, where the temp cue signals thermometer tradition. In work threads 🌡️ Thermometer lives as a quick coded check-in. Across all of these surfaces the rule is the same: the more activity the moment, the more natural 🌡️ feels.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip the Thermometer emoji in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The thermometer-coded cue is the wrong register for somber moments. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid the Thermometer emoji in formal or professional contexts where the activity energy feels off. A plain check-in or a sentence keeps the message grounded.

Skip the Thermometer emoji when you want to communicate something abstract. The Thermometer register is too thermometer-coded for emotional moments; use a heart or sentence when the moment needs warmth.
